findings.evidence: `rg RealClosure mathlib/Mathlib` returns no hits, so this is not a Mathlib namespace; every other project-owned namespace in `TauCeti/FieldTheory` is nested under `TauCeti` (`Minpoly/IsIntegrallyClosedIn.lean:52`, `KummerExtension.lean:46`, `IntermediateField/Quadratic.lean:40`).
findings.fix: Wrap each file in `namespace TauCeti` (i.e. `TauCeti.RealClosure`), matching the repo convention, e.g. `code/TauCeti/GroupTheory/TriangleGroup/Regular.lean:46-48` (`namespace TauCeti` then `namespace TriangleGroup`).
findings.issue: `namespace RealClosure` is a new top-level namespace holding Tau Ceti's own notions (`weightedSquares`, `extensionCone`, `OrderedSubfield`, all the `exists_*` theorems); none is dot notation on a Mathlib type. Same in OrderedSubfield.lean:20, PolynomialCone.lean:20, OddExtension.lean:26, Basic.lean:31.

findings.evidence: `roadmap/TauCetiRoadmap/RealAlgebraicGeometry/Suggested.lean:26` states the identical signature under `exists_realClosure`; README line 136: "The checked target is `exists_realClosure`".
findings.fix: Rename to `exists_realClosure` (the roadmap target name); keep `exists_intermediateField` or rename it `exists_isRealClosed_intermediateField` so its conclusion is visible.
findings.issue: `exists_ordered_extension` understates the conclusion: the statement gives an algebraic, real closed, strictly ordered extension, not merely an ordered one, and the roadmap fixes the name of this exact statement as `exists_realClosure`.

findings.evidence: Mathlib names this conclusion `neg_one_notMem` (`Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Ring/Ordering/Defs.lean:82`, `RingPreordering.neg_one_notMem`) and the totality field `mem_or_neg_mem` (`HasMemOrNegMem`, used at Extension.lean:117); `rg '^(theorem|lemma) \S*proper' mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra` has no such usage.
findings.issue: `quadratic_cone_proper` and `odd_cone_proper` (OddExtension.lean:53) conclude `-1 ∉ extensionCone …`; `proper` is not Mathlib vocabulary for this, and the same holds for the structure field `OrderedSubfield.neg_one` (OrderedSubfield.lean:33) and `OrderedSubfield.total` (line 32).

findings.evidence: `Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Ring/Ordering/Defs.lean:76`: `protected theorem mul_self_mem (P : RingPreordering R) (x : R) : x * x ∈ P` (used by this PR at Extension.lean:47).
findings.issue: `square_mem_extensionCone` proves `x * x ∈ extensionCone f`; Mathlib spells this `mul_self_mem`.

findings.evidence: The proof is literally `AddSubmonoid.subset_closure hx`; Mathlib's `AddSubmonoid.mem_closure` is the iff.
findings.issue: `mem_extensionCone` is a one-directional `x ∈ weightedSquares f → x ∈ extensionCone f`; in Mathlib `mem_foo` is the membership characterisation and the generator inclusion is `subset_closure`.

findings.evidence: Naming conventions: "the name of theorem simply describes the conclusion", hypotheses after `of_`; contrast `nonneg_of_mem_extensionCone` at OrderExtension.lean:94.
findings.issue: `extensionCone_degree`, `extensionCone_eval` (line 61), `extensionCone_map` (line 69), and `extensionCone_nonneg` (OrderExtension.lean:74) name the hypothesis, not the conclusion (`Even natDegree ∧ 0 ≤ leadingCoeff`, `0 ≤ eval x p`, `aeval x p ∈ extensionCone`, `0 ≤ g x`), while `nonneg_of_mem_extensionCone` in the same PR follows the convention.

findings.evidence: Naming conventions, "Predicates as suffixes": `IsClosed (Icc a b)` is `isClosed_Icc`; Extension.lean:126 already uses `isStrictOrderedRing` for the same conclusion.
findings.issue: `OrderedSubfield.ordered` proves `IsStrictOrderedRing P.field`; the predicate should appear in the name, as the PR itself does for `RingPreordering.isStrictOrderedRing` (Extension.lean:126). Likewise `mem_of_maximal` (line 193) takes `IsMax P`.
`exists_odd_factor` reads as an odd polynomial factor; the conclusion is an irreducible factor of odd degree.

summary: Project-owned notions (OrderedSubfield, extensionCone, weightedSquares) live in a top-level `RealClosure` namespace instead of under `TauCeti`, the headline theorem is named below its strength and differently from the roadmap target, and several lemmas use non-Mathlib terminology (`proper`, `square_mem`, `total`, `neg_one`) or name the hypothesis instead of the conclusion. The `RingPreordering.*` dot-notation lemmas are correctly placed.
